llm.summary: The skill is a real clipboard-recovery helper, but it exposes broad sensitive clipboard access plus persistent and state-changing clipmem controls that deserve review before installation.

dimensions.detail: macOS-local operation and SQLite storage are coherent with the purpose, but continuously archiving every clipboard state is broad local private-data indexing and may include secrets, documents, URLs, file paths, images, and PDFs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation relies on a mutable Homebrew tap or Cargo package for the external clipmem binary without a pinned version, checksum, or included audited implementation, while that binary is expected to handle sensitive clipboard history.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill says to pick narrow commands and use JSON, but it does not provide a clear permission boundary or strong confirmation rules before exposing raw clipboard contents, exporting files, deleting archive entries, or changing persistent settings.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifacts disclose background watcher setup, service start/stop/uninstall, launch-at-login preference bridging, and app preference writes; these are not hidden, but they are persistent host changes with limited explicit user-control guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The recall/search/timeline/get/export workflow matches the stated clipboard-memory purpose, but the bundled references also document hard delete, purge, service management, app preference changes, launch-at-login, update checks, and agent skill install/uninstall commands beyond simple recall.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the clipmem publisher and are comfortable with a persistent local clipboard archive. Before using it, restrict agents to read-only recall/search/timeline/get workflows where possible, require explicit confirmation for export, restore, delete, purge, setup, service, settings, launch-at-login, update-check, and install/uninstall commands, and avoid broad searches when the clipboard may contain passwords, tokens, private documents, or other sensitive data.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the artifact is a skill wrapper around the clipmem CLI, so it is not required to implement recall itself; the setup script is disclosed as an auxiliary health check.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the command reference documents destructive and administrative surfaces such as forget, purge, service control, settings mutation, and app controls that exceed read-focused clipboard recall.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in part: settings reset, app controls, and OpenClaw/Hermes install or uninstall commands are management capabilities rather than necessary recall operations.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted: the skill lacks an explicit allowed-command or confirmation boundary despite access to highly sensitive clipboard history and mutable controls.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a guardrail gap: accessing clipboard contents is the core purpose, but the artifacts do not prominently warn that recalled or exported data may contain secrets or personal information.
[RA2] unexpected: Accepted in part: service and launch-at-login controls can create cross-session behavior; they are disclosed, but they broaden a recall skill's authority.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: app update-check run is a documented live network-capable operation, which is not expected for a local clipboard-recall workflow.
[EA2] unexpected: Downgraded: I found no instruction to autonomously execute destructive actions, but the mutation commands would benefit from explicit confirmation requirements.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: depending on an unpinned external clipmem binary is a material supply-chain concern because the binary is intended to run persistently and process sensitive clipboard data.
